stories.title: Academic who accused Cambridge professor of plagiarism suspended
stories.summary:
Nathan Cofnas, the postdoctoral researcher who led plagiarism allegations against former Cambridge professor Jason Arday, has been suspended by Ghent University in Belgium. The suspension is pending a disciplinary investigation into his conduct.

Cofnas's accusations preceded Arday's resignation and subsequent death. He was previously dismissed from Cambridge in 2024 over his views on race.

The researcher is described as an outspoken critic of diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.

stories.summary:

The transfer followed a court order, according to Al Jazeera. Khan, who was voted out of office in April 2022, has remained in prison for more than three years.

stories.title: ISIS Supporter Arrested In Plot To Bomb New York State Capitol
stories.summary:
Federal prosecutors announced the arrest of a woman accused of plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol in Albany. Jessica Bowie, 35, was charged with attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

According to federal authorities, Bowie allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and communicated with an undercover FBI source posing as an ISIS facilitator. The charges stem from her alleged efforts to further the goals of the extremist group through planned violence against a state government building.

stories.title: Hong Kong Tiananmen activists found guilty of national security charges
stories.summary:
Hong Kong activists associated with Tiananmen Square commemorations have been found guilty of national security charges under the law introduced by China. The verdict marks a significant escalation in the enforcement of Beijing's security framework within the territory.

According to BBC reporting, three activists were accused of inciting others to subvert state power. The charges stem from activities related to the annual June 4th anniversary events that have been heavily restricted in recent years.

An activist group criticized the outcome, describing the Hong Kong judicial system as "twisted" and asserting that the verdict had been predetermined. This framing highlights ongoing tensions between local civil society groups and the authorities implementing national security measures.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-LA) stated that Democrats are planning to impeach President Trump if their party takes control of the U.S. House of Representatives in November, describing such action as coming "Day One."

stories.title: Trump tells Michael Cohen he was ‘weaponized’ in hush money trial
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump said his former attorney Michael Cohen was “weaponized” during a surprise radio interview, marking their first public conversation in nearly a decade. The remarks came as Trump praised Cohen for retracting testimony he gave in the 2024 hush money trial.

The two men’s relationship has shifted dramatically over time. It began with a close lawyer-client alliance and later turned into a public feud after Cohen became a central witness against Trump in legal proceedings.

Trump framed the episode as evidence of broader abuse, arguing that both the justice system and mainstream media had been used against Cohen. The interview offered a rare on-record reconciliation between two figures who once played opposing roles in one of the most closely watched political trials in recent years.

President Donald Trump announced a new economic campaign against Iran on Wednesday, which he labeled “ECONOMIC D-DAY.” In a Truth Social post, the president compared his strategy to the World War II Normandy invasion and warned of severe consequences for nations that continue doing business with Tehran.

The announcement framed the move as an all-out effort to dismantle what Trump called Iran’s shadow economy. He criticized the Iranian government for refusing diplomatic engagement, stating that the period for polite negotiations had ended.

Trump threatened “tremendous economic consequences” for any country providing financial support or trade lifelines to the regime. The declaration marks a significant escalation in U.S. pressure on Tehran through targeted sanctions and international economic isolation.

The watchdog is investigating allegations that he arranged illegal political donations from schools to lobbying companies controlled by the Reformers.

McInerney is described as a key person of interest in the ongoing investigation into alleged Liberal party corruption. His removal comes amid heightened scrutiny over financial dealings between educational institutions and political entities.

Separately, Australian authorities are moving toward allowing citizens to block all online gambling advertisements. The proposed system would enable individuals to register their name, email address, or phone number to prevent seeing such ads across online platforms.

stories.title: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
stories.summary:
Google has introduced a new feature designed to help publishers counter declining traffic caused by AI search. The update provides readers with a button that allows them to designate specific news outlets as preferred sources.

This designation applies across Google Search, Discover, and Google News. By making a publisher their preferred source, users may see more of its content in these platforms.

The move aims to boost direct traffic for publishers at a time when AI-driven search results are sending fewer clicks to traditional websites.

The developer has previously created games so closely aligned with their protagonists that they influenced film adaptations, including this year's Spider-Man movie.

stories.summary:
Education Secretary Sonny Angara visited public schools in the Negros Island Region on Thursday to evaluate campus safety protocols and assess facility conditions. The Department of Education said the inspections were part of an effort to engage directly with students and teachers while reviewing school environments.

Among the stops was Bais City National High School, described as the largest secondary school in the area. Angara’s visit focused on discussing campus safety measures with local school communities.

stories.title: Leading China Property Developer Reports Huge loss, in Sign of Widening Real-Estate Woes
stories.summary:
Vanke, one of China's leading property developers, has reported a huge loss. The result underscores the widening nature of the country's real estate crisis.

The developer's troubles raise questions about how far the sector's problems may continue to spread. They also highlight uncertainty over whether the Chinese state will intervene to support the industry.

stories.title: Someone targeted security researchers using a fake crypto conference as a lure
stories.summary:
A hacker targeted cybersecurity professionals by posing as an employee of a leading cryptocurrency news website. The attacker used a fake crypto conference as a lure to reach security researchers.

The campaign relied on Google Docs links to deliver malware to the victims. TechCrunch reported that several cybersecurity experts were specifically targeted in the operation.

stories.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop 8 review: a quality PC whose trackpad taps you back
stories.summary:
Microsoft has released the Surface Laptop 8, a direct successor to the 2024 seventh edition that marked the company's shift to ARM-based, Qualcomm-powered hardware. The new model is designed to compete more effectively with Apple's MacBook Air.

The laptop features snappy performance and longer battery life compared to its predecessor. It also includes an improved keyboard and a new haptic touchpad, which reviewers have noted as standout features for Windows 11 users.

Despite these upgrades, the Surface Laptop 8 comes with a significant price increase. This cost hike is attributed to the high market prices of memory components and chips.

stories.title: Freed Israeli Hostages Still Had Shrapnel in Their Bodies From Oct. 7 Attack
stories.summary:
Freed Israeli hostages returned with shrapnel embedded in their bodies from the October 7 attack, according to an Israeli medical official.

The injuries highlight the physical toll of the initial assault on those who were subsequently taken captive. Some of the women among the freed group had been held alone for extended periods before their release.

These individuals spent eight months in tunnels during their captivity, a detail that underscores the prolonged and difficult conditions they endured.

stories.title: Sennheiser Momentum 5 headphones review: great sound meets exceptional battery life
stories.summary:
Sennheiser’s latest Momentum 5 Bluetooth headphones combine the brand’s established sound quality with improved noise cancelling and a focus on long-term usability. The premium over-ear model is positioned as a direct successor to earlier Momentum releases, aiming to keep pace with competitors in the high-end wireless audio market.

The headphones are priced at £330 (€400/$400/A$749) and emphasize comfort alongside extensive connectivity options. A notable feature is the user-replaceable battery, which Sennheiser presents as a practical upgrade for consumers seeking durability in premium Bluetooth noise-cancelling headphones.
